body.summary: Four rounds of external code review against the completed build (t1-t7) found and fixed 8 real production bugs in src/shared/vibe-adapter.ts and its call sites, none of which this Story's own plan had scoped as Tasks: (1) explicit Vibe chat launched the wrong binary name with the new plain-CLI argv; (2) an exit/close race could finalize on partial stdout and drop a trailing unterminated journal line; (3) removing the old dispatchState retry guard let an edit session replay an already-possibly-mutated turn; (4) history bridging dropped reasoning events and tool-result pairings; (5) cancellation/deadline handling had multiple gaps (checked only post-spawn, not during drain, not during output extraction); (6) extraction-phase parsing failures were wrongly treated as non-retryable; (7) complete()/completeStructuredVibe() inherited the installed CLI's own accept-edits-by-default config instead of explicitly denying tool execution, letting an ordinary completion silently mutate files before an unsafe retry; (8) runVibeTurn could crash the host with an unhandled rejection on an ordinary, fully-handled CLI failure, and the fix for that then risked masking a genuine callback failure as success. All 8 are fixed with regression tests (commits 87b6555ea, bbf649c9c, 5543338ad, fd6fb328a), live-verified against the real installed vibe 3.1.4 binary where behavior was uncertain. The transport contract test was itself strengthened during review round 2 (finding 5): it now scans every production .ts file under src/ and vscode-plugin/src/ rather than 4 hardcoded files, which renamed its second case's title (reflected in the test mapping below). t7's own disclosed gap stands, narrowed by round 2: the full relevant sweep is not 100% green, but every remaining failure is pre-existing/unrelated (Kotlin/native/chat-theme suites) -- the cli-adapter.test.ts gap this packet originally disclosed here is now closed. One documentation-only item remains open and is NOT a code defect: the approved LLD's ac4 wording ("two attempts", a typed error) still doesn't match the intentionally-preserved, pre-existing three-attempt/generic-Error structured-retry behavior -- disclosed for the user's decision at approval (accept-with-note, or a follow-up LLD amendment), not something this build or its review-response rounds could fix off-ledger.
